definition.en-US: A program that stores organized data so that the data is still there after the app that uses it stops.

analogy.en-US: Like a well-kept filing cabinet, where every folder stays in its drawer even after the office closes for the night.

definition.en-US: The part of an app that runs in the browser and shows the page, the buttons and the forms that you use.

analogy.en-US: Like the dining room of a restaurant, where you see the tables and the menu but not the kitchen.

definition.en-US: The part of an app that runs on a server, receives requests, saves and reads data, and sends back a reply.

analogy.en-US: Like the kitchen behind the counter, which prepares every order that comes in from the dining room.

definition.en-US: A numbered door on a computer that a program listens on for connections, such as 5432 for PostgreSQL.

analogy.en-US: Like the room number of one office in a large building, so that a visitor knows exactly which door to knock on.

definition.en-US: A set of rows and columns in a database that holds one kind of thing, such as all the guestbook messages.

analogy.en-US: Like one page of a paper ledger, with a line for each item and a box for each detail.

definition.en-US: A set of addresses and rules that lets one program ask another program for data or ask it to do something.

analogy.en-US: Like a restaurant menu, which lists what you may order without showing you the kitchen.

definition.en-US: A short written description of what you want an app to do, which the AI reads before it writes any code.

analogy.en-US: Like the notes a customer hands a builder before any work begins.

definition.en-US: A plain text file named .env, with lines of the form NAME=value, that Docker Compose reads to fill in its settings.

analogy.en-US: Like a sticky note in a drawer that lists the codes you need, kept apart from the instructions for building the house.

definition.en-US: A named part of a table that holds one kind of value in every row, and has a data type that limits what it accepts.

analogy.en-US: Like a labelled box on a form, which accepts only the kind of answer its label asks for.

definition.en-US: A running list of messages that a program writes about what it is doing, including the errors it meets.

analogy.en-US: Like the logbook a ship's crew writes in every hour, which shows what happened and when.

definition.en-US: A password, key or other piece of data that gives access to something and must not be shared or stored in source code.

analogy.en-US: Like the key to your house, which opens the door for anyone who holds it, so you keep it in your pocket and not under the doormat.

definition.en-US: A copy of your data, kept in another place, so that you can restore it if the original is lost or damaged.

analogy.en-US: Like a photocopy of an important letter, kept in a different drawer in case the original is lost.
